newsitem.title: USA: Best assigns Allstate Floridian B++ rating.
newsitem.headline: Best assigns Allstate Floridian B++ rating.

text.p: A.M. Best Co said Tuesday it has assigned Allstate Floridian Insurance Co an initial rating of B++ (Very Good).
Allstate Floridian is a recently formed subsidiary of Allstate Insurance Co dedicated only to Florida properties.
A.M. Best said the rating reflects the company's conservative operating leverage, and the financial flexibility and operating support of its parent company.
Allstate Floridian's "secure" rating assignment reflects A.M. Best's believe that the company will be adequately capitalized to supports its exposure to catastrophes.

Allstate Floridian's initial capitalization of $45 million will be increased gradually to $450 million during the next year as policies are renewed into the new company beginning this month, Best said.
Based on past catastrophes, A.M. Best said it expects Allstate Floridian's premium leverage will remain below one times surplus for its first several years of operations.
Partially offsetting these strengths is the company's high exposure to catastrophe, and an unfavorable geographic and production concentration, Best said.
The company's pretax catastrophe leverage before reinsurance is high, equating to about four times surplus, Best said.

Although the catastrophe leverage after reinsurance is also high, Best said that concern is mitigated by the conservative capitalization, and the strength and support of Allstate Floridian's parent company, which provides a substantial amount of the reinsurance.
